clusters.pick_reason: #2410 makes a single, composable API change (TextIO | int for errlog) that fixes the problem for Jupyter users and any other context where a real fd is needed, without adding environment-detection logic that can break as IPython internals evolve. It also updates both stdio_client and _create_platform_compatible_process signatures consistently and touches win32/utilities.py for platform parity. #2020's Jupyter-specific detection can be layered on top later if desired, but the type-widening in #2410 is the necessary foundation either way.

members.title: feat: support stderr logging in Jupyter notebook environments
members.author: BabyChrist666
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2410: sys.stderr is not always a valid argument for subprocess stderr= — in Jupyter kernels, sys.stderr is an IPython output stream (not a real file descriptor), which breaks stdio_client when passed to the subprocess spawner. Both PRs address this root cause: #2020 by auto-detecting Jupyter and switching behavior, #2410 by widening errlog's type to accept integer file descriptors (e.g. subprocess.DEVNULL) so callers can pass a valid fd directly.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #2554's _annotation_accepts_str predicate is more targeted: it skips pre-parsing only when the annotation is exclusively str (plus None), preserving JSON pre-parsing for mixed-primitive unions like str | int where coercion to int is correct. PR #2032's broader _SIMPLE_TYPES approach would silently disable pre-parsing for all simple-type unions, potentially breaking callers who pass '42' to a str | int parameter and expect integer coercion.
